26-md06a-bm-1339.solution: Relative error = absolute error ÷ measured value = 0.5 ÷ 25 = 0.02. As a percentage that is 0.02 × 100 = 2%.
26-md06a-bm-1339.trick: Double both numbers: 0.5 ÷ 25 becomes 1 ÷ 50, which is 2 out of 100, so 2%.

26-md06a-bm-1343.solution: Efficiency = 0.80 × 0.55 = 0.44. Taking 750 MW as the electrical output, heat input = 750 ÷ 0.44 ≈ 1,704.5 MW, so heat dumped = 1,704.5 − 750 ≈ 954.5 MW. In one day (86,400 s) that is 954.5 × 10⁶ W × 86,400 s ≈ 8.25 × 10¹³ J.
26-md06a-bm-1343.trick: Output per day is 750 × 86,400 ≈ 6.5 × 10¹³ J. Efficiency is under 50%, so more heat is dumped than electricity made, and the answer must be bigger than that. Only 8.25 × 10¹³ J is.

26-md06a-bm-1347.solution: A ratio of 1:4 means 1 nurse for every 4 patients. So nurses = 34 ÷ 4 = 8.5. You cannot have half a nurse, so round up to 9 nurses.
26-md06a-bm-1347.trick: 32 patients need 8 nurses, and the 2 left over still need a 9th nurse.

26-md06b-qb-2261.solution: Each hour the amount is multiplied by 0.5. After 2 hours it is 300 × 0.5² = 300 × 0.25 = 75 mg.

26-md06b-qb-2300.solution: Cost before discount = 8 × $20 = $160. A 10% discount leaves 90%, so the total is 0.9 × $160 = $144.

26-md06b-qb-2306.solution: A 1:100 scale means the real size is 100 times the model. So the real height = 15 cm × 100 = 1,500 cm. Dividing by 100 to get metres gives 15 m.
26-md06b-qb-2306.trick: On a 1:100 scale, centimetres on the model become metres in real life, so 15 cm is 15 m.

26-md06b-qb-2390.solution: The inlet fills 1/3 of the tank per hour and the outlet empties 1/4 per hour. Net rate = 1/3 − 1/4 = 4/12 − 3/12 = 1/12 per hour. Time to fill = 1 ÷ (1/12) = 12 hours.
26-md06b-qb-2390.trick: Multiply the two times and divide by their difference: (3 × 4) ÷ (4 − 3) = 12 hours.

26-md06b-qb-2417.trick: 10% a year for 2 years is 20% of the principal. So ₦2,000 is one fifth of it, and 5 × 2,000 = ₦10,000.

26-md06b-qb-2427.trick: For ax² + bx + c, the average rate of change between p and q is a(p + q) + b. Here that is 3 × (2 + 6) − 1 = 23.

26-md06b-qb-2443.solution: 10% remaining means 90% has drained: 0.9 × 25,000 = 22,500 L. Time = 22,500 ÷ 500 = 45 minutes.
26-md06b-qb-2443.trick: Emptying the whole tank takes 25,000 ÷ 500 = 50 minutes. Leaving 10% means using 90% of that time: 45.

26-md06b-qb-2453.solution: The rocket is on the ground when h(t) = 0, so −5t² + 50t = 0. Factorising gives −5t(t − 10) = 0, so t = 0 (the launch) or t = 10. It hits the ground at t = 10 s.
26-md06b-qb-2453.trick: Divide −5t² + 50t = 0 by −5t to get t − 10 = 0, so t = 10.

26-md06b-qb-2522.solution: Use the chain rule: the derivative of sin(u) is cos(u) × u'. Here u = 3x² + 2x, so u' = 6x + 2. So f'(x) = (6x + 2)cos(3x² + 2x).
26-md06b-qb-2522.trick: Keep the inside, change sin to cos, then multiply by the derivative of the inside, 6x + 2. Only the third option has cos together with 6x + 2.

26-md06b-qb-2626.solution: Taking 600 MW as the useful output at 25% efficiency, the input power = 600 ÷ 0.25 = 2,400 MW. The wasted heat power = 2,400 − 600 = 1,800 MW. Over 1 hour that is 1,800 MW × 1 h = 1,800 MWh.
26-md06b-qb-2626.trick: At 25% efficiency, 1 part is useful and 3 parts are wasted, so the waste is 3 × 600 = 1,800 MWh.

26-md06b-qb-2636.solution: 5 machines make 5 gadgets in 5 minutes, so each machine makes 1 gadget in 5 minutes. With 100 machines working at once, 100 gadgets take the same 5 minutes. The answer is 5 minutes.
26-md06b-qb-2636.trick: One machine makes one gadget in 5 minutes. Multiply machines and gadgets by 100 together and the time does not change.

26-md06b-qb-2644.solution: After t hours the culture is multiplied by \(2^{t/2}\). Set \(2^{t/2} = 10\), so t ÷ 2 = log₂10 = ln 10 ÷ ln 2 ≈ 2.3026 ÷ 0.6931 ≈ 3.32. So t = 2 × 3.32 ≈ 6.64 hours.
26-md06b-qb-2644.trick: 10 times lies between 8 times (3 doublings, 6 hours) and 16 times (4 doublings, 8 hours). Only 6.64 hours falls between 6 and 8.

26-md06b-qb-2652.solution: Take interest on the reducing balance at 6% ÷ 12 = 0.5% a month. Then n = −ln(1 − Pr ÷ PMT) ÷ ln(1 + r) = −ln(1 − 8,000 × 0.005 ÷ 400) ÷ ln(1.005) = −ln(0.9) ÷ ln(1.005) ≈ 21.1. After 21 payments about $50 is still owed, so a small 22nd payment is needed. The answer is 22 payments.
26-md06b-qb-2652.trick: With no interest it would take 8,000 ÷ 400 = 20 payments. Interest adds to that, so the answer must be more than 20. Only 22 is.

26-md06b-bm-2842.solution: Start with 100. After +20% it is 100 × 1.2 = 120. After −20% it is 120 × 0.8 = 96. The net change is 96 − 100 = −4, which is −4%.
26-md06b-bm-2842.trick: Up then down by the same 20% gives (1 + 0.2)(1 − 0.2) = 1 − 0.2² = 0.96, so −4%.

26-md06b-bm-2846.solution: The horizontal component = F cos θ = 100 × cos 30°. Since cos 30° = √3 ÷ 2 ≈ 0.866, this is 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 N.
26-md06b-bm-2846.trick: The angle is from the horizontal, so the horizontal part uses cos: 100 × 0.866 = 86.6 N. The 50 N option is the vertical part, 100 × sin 30°.

26-md06b-bm-2848.solution: Doubling every hour for 6 hours multiplies the count by 2⁶ = 64. So the count = 100 × 64 = 6,400.
26-md06b-bm-2848.trick: 2⁶ = 64, so the answer is 64 followed by two zeros: 6,400.

26-md06b-bm-2886.solution: A 1:250 scale means real length = 250 × model length = 250 × 6 cm = 1,500 cm. Since 100 cm = 1 m, that is 15 m.
26-md06b-bm-2886.trick: Each model centimetre is 250 cm, or 2.5 m, in real life. So 6 × 2.5 = 15 m.

26-md06b-bm-2894.solution: 25% remaining means 75% has drained: 0.75 × 20,000 = 15,000 L. Time = 15,000 ÷ 300 = 50 minutes.

26-md06b-bm-2898.solution: The 30 m base is adjacent to the 75° angle and the cable is the hypotenuse. So cos 75° = 30 ÷ L, which gives L = 30 ÷ cos 75° = 30 ÷ 0.2588 ≈ 115.9 m. The cable is about 116 m.
26-md06b-bm-2898.trick: cos 75° ≈ 0.26, just over a quarter, so the cable is just under 4 × 30 = 120 m. Only 116 m fits.

26-md06b-bm-2902.solution: Integrate the marginal cost: C(q) = ∫(6q − 12) dq = 3q² − 12q + k. The fixed cost is the value at q = 0, so k = 200. At q = 10: C = 3(100) − 12(10) + 200 = 300 − 120 + 200 = ₦380.
26-md06b-bm-2902.trick: Integrate to 3q² − 12q + 200 and put in q = 10: 300 − 120 + 200 = 380.

26-md06b-bm-2908.solution: For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] the determinant is ad − bc. Here that is 2 × 4 − 3 × 1 = 8 − 3 = 5.
26-md06b-bm-2908.trick: Multiply down the main diagonal and subtract the other diagonal: 8 − 3 = 5.

26-md06b-bm-2916.solution: Cross Aa × Aa. The four equally likely offspring are AA, Aa, Aa and aa. With complete dominance, AA and Aa look the same, so 3 show the dominant trait and 1 shows the recessive trait. The phenotypic ratio is 3:1.
26-md06b-bm-2916.trick: Four equal offspring types and only aa shows the recessive trait, so 3:1. The 1:2:1 option is the genotype ratio, not the phenotype ratio.

26-md06b-bm-2924.solution: Energy needed = work done = force × distance. The weight is already a force, 30 N. So E = 30 × 10 = 300 J.
26-md06b-bm-2924.trick: Weight is already in newtons, so energy = 30 × 10 = 300 J with no g needed.

26-qf1-qb-0791.solution: If 70% is absorbed, 100% − 70% = 30% passes through, assuming none is reflected. So the transmitted intensity = 0.30 × 250 = 75 W/m².
26-qf1-qb-0791.trick: 10% of 250 is 25, and 30% is three of those: 75.

26-qf1-qb-0799.solution: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 km ÷ 2 h = 60 km/h. To convert to m/s, multiply by 1,000 ÷ 3,600, which is the same as dividing by 3.6. So 60 ÷ 3.6 ≈ 16.67 m/s.
26-qf1-qb-0799.trick: 60 km/h is 1 km per minute, so the speed is 1,000 m per 60 s ≈ 16.67 m/s.

26-qf1-qb-0813.solution: Let the integers be n, n + 2 and n + 4. Their sum is 3n + 6 = 102, so 3n = 96 and n = 32. The numbers are 32, 34 and 36, so the largest is 36.
26-qf1-qb-0813.trick: 102 ÷ 3 = 34 is the middle number. The largest is 2 more: 36.
